annotationRationale: The problem combines right-triangle lengths with bounded integer solutions. Factor pairs give the main route; checking possible hypotenuse squares provides a different elementary route. Both use segment subtraction to obtain the remaining legs.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, the integer right triangles force BP=16, AP=34, DQ=21, AQ=35, and PQ=15. The perimeter is 84, matching choice A and the key. No statement, choice, or figure conflict is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both factor-pair enumeration and bounded square search are complete elementary routes. Recognizing familiar Pythagorean triples would help find candidates but would still require a completeness argument; no additional route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Pythagorean theorem and bounded integer solutions are appropriately assessed. Segment subtraction is supporting work, and the route-specific factorization and square-root nodes match their respective methods.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Nondegeneracy gives 1≤p≤27 and 1≤d≤29. The same-parity factors must both be even, producing uv=225 and ab=196. Both factor-pair lists are exhaustive; their differences uniquely give p=16 and d=21. Thus AP=34, AQ=35, CP=12, CQ=9, and PQ=15, yielding 84.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Accurately develops LIVE and AoPS Solution 2's difference-of-squares route. The exhaustive lists and explicit geometric bounds are independently written elaborations. Both references are third-party, and source-informed-original is appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why integer right triangles lead to factorization. Parity, halved factors, bounds, and completeness are all explained sufficiently for an AMC 10 learner. No diagram is necessary.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_174 supplies the right-triangle equations; math:integer-diophantine-equations supplies integer restrictions and exhaustive factor enumeration; cnm_152 supplies difference-of-squares factorization; cnm_055 supplies segment subtraction. All four IDs are directly supported.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact CN links for Pythagorean theorem, difference of squares, and segment arithmetic match the steps used. Integer-equation synthesis has no accepted CN link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The method exercises the side-length component of 8.G.B.7 and structural factorization component of A-SSE.A.2, not their entire scope. cnm_055's accepted measurement/comparison links do not directly describe this segment-subtraction task. Integer synthesis has no accepted US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The direct concepts are precise, and their assessed/support roles fit the derivation. No unsupported or missing central concept is evident.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The bounds correctly restrict AP to integers 31 through 40 and AQ to 29 through 40. Every listed squared difference is correct; only 256 and 441 respectively are squares. These give BP=16 and DQ=21, followed by PQ=15 and perimeter 84. Endpoints are correctly excluded.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE supplies the Pythagorean setup, while the candidate explicitly identifies the exhaustive hypotenuse search as its development of the existing route. The source claim is honest, and source-informed-original is appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The finite bounds explain why direct checking is feasible. Both lists are exhaustive, and comparing their entries with consecutive squares is readily reproducible without further prerequisites.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_174 supports the equations; math:integer-diophantine-equations supports the complete bounded search; cnm_075 supports recognizing square roots; cnm_079 supports square bracketing to exclude nonsquares; cnm_055 supports the remaining segment lengths. All five IDs fit.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native links for right triangles, finding square roots, square bracketing, and segment arithmetic match the components used. Integer-equation synthesis remains without an accepted CN link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.B.7 and 8.EE.A.2 overlap the triangle and perfect-square steps. The 8.NS.A.2 link reaches only elementary square bracketing here, not finer irrational approximation. cnm_055's physical-measurement links are not directly exercised; integer synthesis has no US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The direct set accurately records a bounded integer search using square recognition and bracketing. The question-level assessed and support roles remain appropriate.
